title: Breakfast Towers
about: Remembering the simple breakfast tradition of stacking empty milk cartons with friends.
description: This track focuses on one of the smallest State Arts-In traditions that became unexpectedly memorable: stacking empty milk cartons into breakfast towers. What started without rules or planning became part of the rhythm of each morning, surrounded by table chants, laughter, and the occasional cheer for a broken plate. Years later, the memory stands as a reminder that the moments people miss most are often not the biggest performances, but the ordinary traditions shared with friends who felt like home.
lyrics: Sleep still hanging in our eyes.
We'd shuffle through the breakfast line,
Waiting for the sun to rise.
Some grabbed one milk, some grabbed six,
We already knew what came next...
Some mornings it was three of us,
No trophy waiting at the end,
If a plate broke, cheers erupted,
You never think the last time's coming...
It's funny what survives the years,
And what you miss the most.
Just breakfast towers made of milk cartons...
With friends who felt like home.
